title: AlphaEnzyme foundation model guides enzyme retrieval and transaminase engineering
summary: AlphaEnzyme reached a top-1 catalyst retrieval success rate of 30.1% on a time-separated benchmark, against 17.2% for the strongest baseline, and Michaelis constant rank correlations up to 0.64 for enzymes sharing at most 40% identity with the kinetic training set. In prospective transaminase engineering, several prioritized variants exceeded the parent, the best giving a 30.4-fold increase in product signal in a lysate-based assay while retaining (R)-selectivity. The result comes from a bioRxiv preprint (version 2 dated 2026-11-05); the number of variants tested is not given in the abstract.
ai_technology: AlphaEnzyme enzyme foundation model on a structure-grounded enzyme-reaction representation predicting catalytic compatibility, kinetics and mutational response

evidence.tested: Prioritized transaminase variants tested in a lysate-based assay; best 30.4-fold product signal increase over parent.
evidence.unknown: Number of variants tested and purified-enzyme kinetics are not in the abstract; preprint; full text not reviewed.
